title: Premier League to publish Key Match Incidents Panel verdicts on referee decisions
dek: The Premier League will publish full verdicts from its Key Match Incidents Panel on referee and VAR decisions for the first time this season. The panel, comprised of five members including former players and coaches, will have its rulings shared publicly via the league's platforms.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Premier League will publish complete Key Match Incidents Panel verdicts on referee and VAR calls this season, ending a policy of private judgment.
bottom_line: The publication of panel verdicts and official explanations marks a shift toward accountability, though Ifab's refusal to permit live VAR broadcast leaves a gap in the full visibility of how video review influences decisions. Watch whether clubs and fans view the measures as substantive or symbolic.
body: The Premier League will publish the full verdicts of its Key Match Incidents Panel on referee and video assistant referee decisions for the first time this season, according to BBC Sport. Until now, the panel's judgments have remained private, though clubs have periodically leaked the information.

The Key Match Incidents Panel, created by Premier League clubs in 2022, has met since the 2022-23 season to assess every major incident. The panel comprises five members: three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative, and one from Pro Ref, the referees' body. Every major incident is assessed and voted on, with feedback provided to clubs and officials.

Under the new transparency measures, selected direct quotes from the referee or video assistant referee will be published on the Premier League's Match Centre account on X, on the Premier League website, and the Premier League app. Previously, the league account published only a general summary of incidents rather than the real-time explanations and thought processes of officials.

The Premier League is also introducing RefCam, which will broadcast audio between the referee and players for the first time. However, RefCam audio will not be live, nor will it include conversations between the referee and the VAR. RefCam audio will be used in-game one or two times in each round of fixtures.

The International Football Association Board (Ifab) has refused to permit the live broadcast of VAR discussions, limiting full transparency on how video review shapes decisions. The Premier League is continuing discussions with Ifab about allowing more VAR communication to be shared with the public.
Three transparency measures form the package: publishing full KMI Panel judgements, publishing direct explanations of officials, and broadcasting RefCam with audio.
